feature: Animate a picture by setting moments and changing things
summary: Pick a layer, press Add Key or K, and change things: each change keys itself at the playhead and the picture tweens between keys. Videos get the same Add Key button.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Draw two shapes on a blank picture.

try.do: Click a shape, then press Add Key in the Motion section, or K.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the shape. The hollow diamond fills in and a Position row appears.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the ruler at 1s. A hollow diamond stands at the playhead.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Drag the shape somewhere else, then set Opacity to 30.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Space. It plays and repeats. Press Space again to stop.
Drag a different shape, one with no keys. It moves for the whole picture.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click the Rotation row on a turning layer, then drag the crosshair.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Click each key on the bar and press Delete. The timeline goes, and it is a still.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

evaluate: After the first key, did you know to move the playhead, or did you stall? The brief said to tell us if you did.
Does the hollow diamond at the playhead tell you where the next change will land before you make it?
Dragging a layer with no keys moves it for the whole picture. Did that ever surprise you?
Is Rotation's pivot easy enough to find, now it only shows with the Rotation row picked?
A still export shows the first moment. Would you rather it showed the moment the playhead is on?
rough: From first click to playing took 16.2 seconds in a walk with two seconds of looking before each of its seven actions. That pace is scripted: nobody new has been timed.
After the first key nothing says to move the playhead. The Icons guide now teaches it, and the brief asked you to say if you stall there.
A key at 0:00 stands 6 points right of the playhead, the same as on the video timeline, whose lanes clip at their edge. Centring it there cut the diamond in half, so I left it.
The mock's diamond and time in the size pill are not built yet: the-size-pill-says-the-key-and-the-time-while-a.
The video mock draws Animate a property where Add Key now stands, and the bell mock draws the pivot from the start: your call on 2026-11-05.
The Lens has no letter now, only its tool bar button and menu row: your call on 2026-11-05.
A still PNG, Copy and a still SVG show the first moment, not the moment the playhead is on.
14 walks pin next-picture-keys off, because saved From and To rows still show and those walks are the only proof of them.
Rotation's Around dropdown is not on the keyed row. The pivot is moved by dragging the crosshair with the row picked.
K itself was pressed through the walk's stand-in for the menu bar, because a walk cannot reach a live menu. Please press it by hand once.
